title: Flash tabs: auto-cleanup kept tabs after idle timeout

Evaluate options before implementing — this may not be worth the complexity

brief.why: When a multi-step script fails mid-way, the tab is destroyed — all page state lost. Claude must re-run the entire script to get back to the failure point. title: wait-idle pauses until network requests settle

title: Auto-wait validated against genuinely slow-hydrating SPA

brief.why: All auto-wait tests used pages that were stable on first poll (~110ms). We don't know if the dual-signal probe (element count + text length) actually catches real hydration — content appearing 500ms+ after load. Usage analysis found Claude wrote 'wait 500'/'wait 1000'/'wait 1500' guesses ~6 times; every one is a proxy for 'wait until the page is actually ready.' Two related capabilities need validation here: (1) DOM-stability auto-wait after goto, (2) network-idle wait for after-click SPA route changes. These are different signals — DOM stability is about element count/text, network idle is about in-flight XHR/fetch calls. passe-tiwuko validates the first; wait-idle (new action) addresses the second.
brief.what: 1. Find or build a page that hydrates slowly (500ms+ after load event) — good candidate: a React or Next.js app that fetches data client-side after mount 2. Run passe fetch against it, observe auto-wait behaviour in step NDJSON (look at ms values and whether content is present) 3. If DOM-stability probe misses hydration, investigate: is the gap between load event and probe installation the issue? 4. Also test: SPA client-side route change via click — does auto-wait fire? (It shouldn't — auto-wait only triggers after goto/back/forward, not click) 5. Document findings and workarounds (wait-for selector, wait-idle)
brief.done: Auto-wait tested against a page with >500ms hydration time. Either probe catches it (with step timing as evidence) or limitations documented with concrete workarounds. SPA click-navigation behaviour confirmed and documented in CLAUDE.md footguns.

title: Daemon module captures all tabs with reconnection

brief.why: Continuous multi-tab capture is the core value from chrome-log. Needs its own WebSocket handler — CDPClient is single-session request-response, daemon is multi-session streaming. Different shapes.
brief.what: READ references/chrome-log-absorption.md FIRST — it has the JSONL schema, DAG placement, and critical gotchas. DO NOT extend CDPClient — write your own WebSocket handler (see reference doc for why: CDPClient is single-session request-response, daemon is multi-session continuous streaming — different shapes, concurrent WebSocket connections to same Chrome are fine). 1. Create src/passe/log_daemon.py with main() entry point (subprocess.Popen, NOT os.fork — asyncio+fork is undefined behavior) 2. Refactor connection.py: extract discover_chrome(cdp_url) that returns (ws_url, browser_info) without creating CDPClient. connect() calls it internally — no behavior change. Daemon calls it directly 3. Daemon should NOT auto-launch Chrome (unlike connect()). Fail loudly if Chrome unreachable 4. Own async WebSocket message loop routing by sessionId field (flattened sessions — all tabs on one socket) 5. Target.setAutoAttach(autoAttach=True, flatten=True) + Target.setDiscoverTargets for multi-tab 6. Port request assembly from chrome-log daemon.py: correlate requestWillBeSent, requestWillBeSentExtraInfo (has Cookie header), responseReceived, responseReceivedExtraInfo (has Set-Cookie), loadingFinished by requestId 7. Network.enable with LARGE BUFFERS: maxTotalBufferSize 100MB, maxResourceBufferSize 50MB, maxPostDataSize 64KB — without these, getResponseBody silently fails on streaming responses 8. Port filtering skip-lists from chrome-log (analytics URLs, file extensions, binary MIME) 9. Body capture via Network.getResponseBody on loadingFinished, 100KB max, base64 decode 10. Write shared JSONL schema to ~/.passe/logs/requests.jsonl with 100MB rotation (3 rotated files) 11. Reconnection state machine (NEW CODE, not a port — chrome-log just exits): on WebSocket close, abandon in-flight requests, backoff 1s/2s/4s...60s cap, re-discover_chrome, re-attach all tabs, re-Network.enable per session, reset backoff on success. SIGTERM = graceful shutdown, no reconnect 12. PID file at ~/.passe/.daemon.pid, pause flag at ~/.passe/logs/.paused 13. NOTE: log_query.py read_requests loads entire file into memory. For daemon logs near 100MB rotation limit this could be millions of entries. Consider streaming with early-exit for tail/limit, or accept the cost since rotation caps individual files. 14. Test: mock WebSocket with canned CDP event sequences, verify JSONL output. Test reconnection by closing mock WS
brief.done: Daemon captures requests across all tabs on local headless and remote Mac Chrome via tailscale. Survives brief tailscale disconnects and reconnects. Log file readable by query tools. Filtering removes analytics noise.

title: Screenshot survives long CDP sessions without compositor timeout

brief.why: Brisk-bear reported screenshot timeouts after sustained CDP use. Investigation found three issues: (1) PASSE_CDP pointed at remote Mac Chrome via tailscale — DPR=2 Retina meant 4× pixels plus multi-MB base64 over network, misidentified as compositor stalls. (2) CDPClient.send had a hardcoded 15s timeout — too short for full-page screenshots of dense pages on software-rendered headless Chrome (Wikipedia NASA: 136s at DPR=1). (3) Headless Chromium on kube was using software rasterisation despite a GTX 1650 SUPER being available — Debian's blocklist disabled GPU.
brief.what: 1. CDPClient.send() accepts per-call timeout parameter (committed) 2. Screenshot capture timeout set to 300s — detect dead browser, don't cap rasterisation (committed) 3. Headless Chrome GPU enabled via --ignore-gpu-blocklist --use-angle=vulkan in systemd service — Wikipedia NASA drops from 136s to 2s (applied to service, documented in CLAUDE.md) 4. Filed passe-zomeca under passe-mofuco — passe should report which Chrome it connects to
brief.done: CDPClient.send accepts timeout parameter. Screenshot uses 300s timeout. Kube headless Chrome GPU-accelerated (2s for Wikipedia NASA). 30-site soak test: 0 failures. CLAUDE.md documents the setup.
